trigger: Chegg CEO says student interest in ChatGPT hurt new customer growth
label_notes: ChatGPT was already public and directly answered study questions and helped with assignments, which is Chegg's main paid use. Chegg's management reported an effect on customer intake. Chegg's own library of verified solutions adds value but is not essential for typical answers.

trigger: OpenAI products for marketing and contracts
label_notes: OpenAI showed agents it really uses internally for leads, support and extracting data from contracts, but did not release them as external CRM or marketing products. These functions overlap with SaaS, while customer records, integrations and full processes remain with enterprise systems.

trigger: Early version of Google Project Genie for creating virtual worlds
label_notes: Project Genie was a research prototype available to a limited group of subscribers, with interactive worlds lasting up to 60 seconds, not a finished video game. It did not replace game mechanics, stories, network infrastructure or publishers' own content.

The available Claude Cowork plugin really did review contracts and NDAs and prepare legal materials, which is part of the paid legal-tech work. It did not replace the full range of professional research, verified case-law databases or specialised vendor data.

trigger: OpenAI approves its first AI insurance app
label_notes: Insurify released an app in ChatGPT for finding and comparing car insurance offers, which overlaps with retail insurance broking. It does not replace corporate broking, complex risk placement or claims service, and quotes need partner and insurer data.

Hazel already gave financial advisers tax analysis from returns and client documents, automating one paid advisory process. It did not replace custody, trade execution or client relationships. It needed personal and custodial data, which are not necessarily exclusive to incumbents.

trigger: Fears that AI will take white-collar jobs
label_notes: There was no specific AI product replacing CBRE or JLL services or the business of office REITs. The event reflected a forecast of lower office employment and property demand. Data on leases, properties and deals may be partly exclusive, but no direct product competition appeared.

trigger: Claim that a tool handles 400% more freight without more staff
label_notes: SemiCab claimed live client deployments and automation of planning, freight coordination and exception handling, which directly affects brokerage operations. It does not replace physical haulage, rail networks or parcel delivery. Its efficiency relies on access to operating data and integrations.

Claude Code Security launched only as a limited research preview that analysed source code for vulnerabilities and suggested patches. This overlaps with application security but does not replace endpoint monitoring, network defence or incident response, which use their own telemetry and threat intelligence.

The already available Claude Code was presented as a tool for analysing and migrating COBOL code. Anthropic launched no separate modernisation product that day. This touches part of software rewriting services but does not replace IBM mainframes, transaction reliability or integration of complex systems.

trigger: Leaked draft documents describe a more powerful Claude model
label_notes: On the event date there was only a leak of draft documents with claims about the cyber capabilities of the unreleased Claude Mythos/Capybara model. No proven available product replaced EDR, network defence or vulnerability management. Existing solutions use client telemetry and specialised data.
